facts.claim: GitHub's hosted MCP server is at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
facts.evidence: remote-server.md gives the URL; the protected-resource document at https://api.githubcopilot.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/ names resource https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/.

facts.claim: A personal access token works as Authorization: Bearer
facts.evidence: "manually configure it to use a personal access token (PAT)" with "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT".

facts.claim: The server's OAuth authorization server (github.com/login/oauth) publishes no dynamic registration, so a browser sign-in needs an app the user creates
facts.evidence: authorization_servers is https://github.com/login/oauth; no registration endpoint was found. The docs say OAuth needs the client's OAuth app enabled for organisations with restrictions.

facts.claim: A /readonly path suffix (or the X-MCP-Readonly header) limits the server to read tools
Available to all GitHub users; a tool behind a paid feature needs that subscription
facts.evidence: "available to all GitHub users regardless of plan type"; "tools that interact with Copilot Cloud Agent require a paid Copilot license".

facts.claim: get_me is a read tool with no required arguments (smoke)
facts.evidence: README tool list names get_me ("Get my user profile") with no parameters.

facts.claim: issue_read, pull_request_read, actions_get/list, projects_get/list only read; merge_pull_request, push_files, create_or_update_file, delete_file and the *_write tools change things
facts.evidence: README tool list and parameter descriptions (method values get, get_diff, get_status ... for the *_read tools).

facts.claim: The MCP endpoint is the only host LOTR talks to for a token connection
facts.evidence: The token is sent to https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ only; no sign-in host is involved with a personal access token.
